title: Em Dash (—): Copy & Paste + Why It Became the "AI Writing" Tell
meta_description: Copy and paste the em dash (—), see how it differs from the en dash (–), hyphen, and minus sign, and why it became known as an AI writing tell. Click any symbol to copy it instantly.
hero_tagline: The em dash (—) that marks a break, an interruption, or an aside — the punctuation mark that sparked the 2025 debate over whether long dashes are a sign of AI writing. Click any symbol to copy it instantly.
intro: The em dash (—, Unicode U+2014) is the long dash writers use to set off a sudden break, a dramatic pause, or a parenthetical aside — roughly doing the job of a comma, colon, or pair of parentheses. It's also the character at the center of a running argument about AI-written text, and the one most often mixed up with the shorter en dash and the plain keyboard hyphen.
